To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

children with poor reading fluencies are impaired in change detection for both letter and shape stimuli, indicating that the difference is not specifically due to graphemic or lexical training but more likely reflects an attentional performance difference at the level of pre recognition.
children with dyslexia are less sensitive to visual change than children without dyslexia.
children with poor reading ability have impaired visual attention.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether dyslexic children are less able than their peers to attend selectively to relevant information in their visual environment.
the question of whether there is a common factor that underpins reading ability and other cognitive skills.
the role of attentional processes in the acquisition of reading skills.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
change detection is an important and reliable measure of transient visual attention, and that it may be used to investigate and understand the underlying cause of dyslexia.
the difference in performance is due to the difference in the ability to detect change, rather than the ability to recognize the target.

the results of this study indicate that the difference in performance of the good and poor readers was not specific to letters or graphemic processing, and was instead a result of differences in low level visual processing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dyslexic children have a deficit in the pre recognition stage of visual processing that is independent of the type of stimulus.
change detection is a measure of the ability to focus attention on a target and to ignore distraction.
the good readers have a superior ability to focus on relevant information and suppress irrelevant information, and that this is a critical ability that is necessary for learning to read.
The main takeaway from our work is that
change detection is an important tool for the investigation of dyslexia.
dyslexic and non-dyslexic children differ in the way they process visual information.
dyslexics are not just slow at reading but also slow at detecting changes, and this may be a consequence of a more global attentional deficit.
